rounds.title: Setting Off
rounds.support: A, describe the photo. B, look away and ask: Who is there? What are they doing? What are they taking?
rounds.challenge: A, describe clues about the journey. B, look away and question possible reasons for travelling. Discuss what the photo cannot tell you.

rounds.title: Visits and New Homes
rounds.support: Where would you like to go on holiday? What would you take? Would you take different things when moving to a new home?
rounds.challenge: How might packing for a holiday differ from packing for a permanent move? How could having little time or money affect your choices?

rounds.title: Holiday Club Welcome
rounds.support: A, invite B to a holiday activity. B, ask about it. C, suggest an activity. Swap A and B halfway.
rounds.challenge: Agree on an activity that feels welcoming. Discuss cost, language and unfamiliar rules. C, introduce a difficulty and help both roles find a solution.
roles: A holiday club member welcoming someone
A teenager who recently moved here

rounds.title: Time Together
rounds.support: A, describe the photo. B, look away and ask: Where are they? What are they doing? How could someone new join?
rounds.challenge: A, describe the scene. B, look away and ask questions. Discuss how this activity could build friendships and what might make joining difficult.
rounds.imageQuery2: adults cooking together in community kitchen

rounds.title: Finding Common Ground
rounds.support: Ask B and C: What helps you feel at home? What could you share with someone new during the holidays? Swap A and B halfway.
rounds.challenge: Ask B and C: What connects holiday travel and migration? Where does that comparison fail? How can shared experiences build empathy without assuming identical lives?

rounds.title: A Fair Holiday Trip
rounds.support: A, suggest a holiday outing. B, explain what you enjoy and can spend. Agree on a plan. Swap roles halfway.
rounds.challenge: Negotiate an outing both classmates can enjoy. Discuss budget, transport and preferences without making assumptions. Justify your choices and agree on a fair compromise.
roles: A student planning a holiday outing
A classmate who recently moved here
